title: When the Gravity Burns Revisited
premise: Sebastian Whitlock, a terraformer and cargo hauler in the contested orbits of Kepler Station, discovers his name on the manifest of the Meridian, a ship that was destroyed fifteen years ago — the same ship whose crash erased his memory of who he really was. The manifest lists a passenger: Ilsa Vane, daughter of the warlord who now rules both fleets, carrying a message Sebastian unknowingly delivered before the crash. As Vane's agents close in, Sebastian must reconstruct his lost identity through fragments of memory, old crewmates, and the garden he tends for colonists not yet born, realizing he was the courier chosen precisely because no one would suspect a man with nothing to lose. In the end, Sebastian delivers the message — proof of Vane's father's original peace accord — to the last neutral council, ending the war but costing him the anonymity he treasured; he chooses to stay on Kepler Station, finally belonging somewhere, as the first generation of colonists arrives to walk his garden.
about_author: R. M. Thackeray is the pen name of a former logistics analyst who spent a decade writing shipping manifests before turning them into fiction. They live somewhere with real weather and write about people who keep systems running while history happens overhead.

chapters.title: The Manifest That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: POV Sebastian. While reconciling cargo records at Kepler Station, Sebastian finds his own name on the manifest of the Meridian, destroyed fifteen years ago — listed alongside an unfamiliar passenger, Ilsa Vane. He assumes a clerical error. Emotional beat: quiet unease beneath routine, the first crack in a carefully invisible life.

chapters.title: Fifteen Years of Hauling Nothing Important
chapters.summary: POV Sebastian. Flashback-tinged chapter establishing Sebastian's daily life: hauling cargo, tending the orbital greenhouse meant for future colonists, keeping his head down since waking from the Meridian crash with amnesia. A station archivist mentions someone has been pulling his personnel file. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as contentment.

chapters.title: A Name Like a Loaded Gun
chapters.summary: POV Sebastian. He researches Ilsa Vane and learns she is the estranged daughter of Admiral Corvus Vane, whose fleet blockade strangles both sides of the war. Worse: archives show Ilsa boarded the Meridian the day it crashed — and survived, officially dead ever since. Emotional beat: dread hardening into purpose.

chapters.title: The Garden for People Not Yet Born
chapters.summary: POV Sebastian. Tending seedlings engineered for planets still being terraformed, Sebastian confronts why he stayed: the garden is the only thing he's certain he loves. An old crewmate, Dara Okonkwo, visits and goes pale when he describes the manifest. Emotional beat: tenderness as anchor against rising fear.

chapters.title: What Dara Remembers
chapters.summary: POV Dara. Dara recalls the Meridian's final run: Sebastian carried a sealed case he never opened, given by a dying stranger at a fuel depot. She never told him because the doctors warned recovered memories could break him. Emotional beat: guilt of long silence, loyalty tested.

chapters.title: Visitors in Contested Orbit
chapters.summary: POV Sebastian. Two 'insurance investigators' arrive asking about the Meridian's cargo. Their questions are too precise; their ship transponder belongs to Vane's fleet. Sebastian lies smoothly and realizes lying came easily — a skill from a life he can't remember. Emotional beat: the hunter becoming visible.

chapters.title: The Case Under the Seedlings
chapters.summary: POV Sebastian. Searching his own quarters' hidden seams — habits his hands remember — Sebastian finds a stasis-sealed case embedded in the greenhouse foundation, placed there by his past self. Inside: documents bearing Vane's own seal. Emotional beat: vertigo of meeting your own foresight.

chapters.title: Corvus Vane's Long War
chapters.summary: POV interlude, omniscient-historical. A compressed history of how Admiral Vane manufactured the war to consolidate power over both fleets, and how a peace faction led by his wife was purged — the same week the Meridian fell. Emotional beat: cold clarity; the war is a machine with one owner.

chapters.title: Ilsa, Alive and Looking
chapters.summary: POV Ilsa. Introduced at last: living under a false name in the outer yards, Ilsa has spent fifteen years hunting proof her mother's peace accord existed. She sent the query that surfaced the manifest, not knowing the courier lived. Emotional beat: hope sharpened by fifteen years of grief.

chapters.title: Two People Chasing One Ghost
chapters.summary: POV alternating Sebastian/Ilsa. Their paths converge via Dara, who contacts Ilsa's network. First encrypted contact between Sebastian and Ilsa: wary, transactional, each testing whether the other is bait. Emotional beat: two strangers recognizing themselves in each other's damage.

chapters.title: The Investigators Return
chapters.summary: POV Sebastian. Vane's agents stop pretending, seizing the station's dock authority and demanding Sebastian's files. Dara covers his escape through the cargo bays; a dockworker friend is detained. Emotional beat: the cost of invisibility ending — allies exposed one by one.

chapters.title: Memory in Fragments
chapters.summary: POV Sebastian. Under stress, Sebastian's memories surface in shards: a woman's voice reading the accord aloud, his own promise to deliver it 'even if I forget why.' He understands he volunteered for a memory-wipe protocol so no interrogation could extract the message. Emotional beat: grief and awe at his past self's sacrifice.

chapters.title: The Neutral Council of Ceres Reach
chapters.summary: POV Ilsa. Ilsa explains the plan: the case holds the signed original accord plus evidence of Vane's purge orders. Only the Neutral Council can authenticate and broadcast it. But the council convenes in nine days, and Vane's fleet controls every approach. Emotional beat: a plan that is really a gamble.

chapters.title: Buying a Ship with a Lie
chapters.summary: POV Sebastian. Using his spotless fifteen-year hauler record, Sebastian wins a legitimate contract whose route passes near Ceres Reach — smuggling himself and Ilsa inside his own cargo. Emotional beat: reclaiming competence; the invisible man weaponizing his invisibility.

chapters.title: Dara Stays Behind
chapters.summary: POV Dara. Dara refuses to come, choosing instead to feed false telemetry to Vane's agents and protect the garden. A farewell scene between her and Sebastian, fifteen years of unspoken care finally spoken. Emotional beat: love expressed as letting go.

chapters.title: Running the Blockade
chapters.summary: POV Sebastian. The run through contested orbit: a near-miss inspection, Ilsa nearly surrendering herself to save the cargo, Sebastian talking their way past a young officer who reminds him of who he used to be. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into resolve.

chapters.title: The Trap at Ceres Reach
chapters.summary: POV Ilsa. Arriving, they find the council chamber already infiltrated — Vane anticipated the accord's survival and plans to destroy it publicly, branding it forgery. Ilsa realizes her father let them come. Emotional beat: despair at an enemy who plays longer games.

chapters.title: What the Message Actually Says
chapters.summary: POV Sebastian. Opening the case fully, they find a personal addendum: Sebastian's pre-wipe testimony, naming witnesses to the purge and explaining why he chose oblivion — because he believed the message mattered more than the messenger. Emotional beat: the climax's moral key; conviction stronger than self.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: POV alternating. Climax: during the council session, Vane's agents move to seize the chamber; Sebastian triggers the station-wide broadcast of the accord, testimony, and purge orders himself, using the hauler's uplink he registered years ago — his invisibility becoming the delivery mechanism. Fleets receive it mid-battle. Emotional beat: catharsis; truth arriving like light after a long dark.

chapters.title: The Fall of Corvus Vane
chapters.summary: POV Ilsa. Both fleets turn on Vane as commanders verify the documents. Confronted by his daughter, Vane offers her succession; she refuses and takes him alive to face the council. Emotional beat: justice without vengeance; breaking a cycle rather than continuing it.

chapters.title: Aftermath of a Man With His Name Back
chapters.summary: POV Sebastian. Offered medals, commissions, a restored identity and history, Sebastian declines all of it. He returns to Kepler Station, where freed dockworkers greet him and Dara waits. Emotional beat: quiet reckoning — you can't be invisible again, but you can choose where to stand.

chapters.title: First Planting
chapters.summary: POV Sebastian, epilogue. The first colony ships arrive carrying the people his garden was grown for. Sebastian walks the new settlers through the greenhouses, teaching them which seedlings are theirs. For the first time, the garden has an audience. Emotional beat: belonging earned, not found — roots finally meeting soil.
